title: Editorial Policy
description: The editorial standards that guide reporting at The Daily Meridian: accuracy, independence, fairness and transparency.
body: The Daily Meridian exists to inform. Our reporting is guided by four principles: accuracy, independence, fairness and transparency.

items: We verify facts before publication and attribute information to its source.
We distinguish clearly between what we know, what we have been told and what we believe to be likely.
Headlines must be supported by the article body and must not exaggerate.
Editorial decisions are made by editors, never by advertisers, sponsors or owners.
Advertising is clearly labelled and visually separated from editorial content.
Journalists declare any conflict of interest to their editor.
We seek comment from people or organisations that are the subject of critical reporting.
We do not use anonymous sources unless there is a strong public interest and the editor knows the source's identity.
Opinion and analysis are clearly labelled and kept separate from news reporting.
Every article shows its author, publication date and the date of the last substantive update.
Corrections are published openly. See our Corrections Policy.
Demonstration or sample content is clearly labelled as such.

body: We use images we own, have licensed, or that are available under licences that permit our use. Image credits are shown in captions. Images are not manipulated in ways that mislead.
Any use of automated tools in producing content is subject to human editorial review. We do not publish AI-generated news reporting as if it were produced by a journalist.
